title: The conceptual-allocation tag could never be set
found: Reading tracer-core.js alongside its only caller.
detail: abstractList() did `const block=t.alloc(...); if(block&&typeof block==="object")block.conceptual=true;` but alloc() returns a NUMERIC block id, so the guard was always false and no heap block was ever tagged. The memory ledger still classified those blocks correctly only because it falls back to matching /pseudocode|conceptual/ against the block's source string, which hid the dead code. A comment in tracer-ui.js even recorded that the flag "was absent".
fix: alloc() accepts an options argument and sets the flag; abstractList passes it. The string fallback is retained for blocks that only declare provenance.
verified: warshall 1/1, dijkstra 3/3, kruskal 2/2 and bfs 1/1 conceptual blocks now carry the flag, matching exactly what the string fallback had been catching, so behaviour is unchanged and the dead code is live.

title: Declared field bounds were never enforced, and seven graph modules had none
found: A systematic sweep of all 134 fields across all 68 modules, run as one subprocess per module so an unbounded field could not hang the sweep.
detail: AUD-03 named only hamilton nV=8. In fact: SEVEN modules (graphadt, bfs, dfs, warshall, dijkstra, kruskal, prim) declared NO nV maximum at all; on ELEVEN more that did declare one, "1e3" and "0x10" passed Number.isInteger and bypassed it, yielding nV=1000 and two 1000x1000 matrices; four modules hung the 25-second sweep at that size. recfactorial, whose max of 12 is the int32 factorial boundary, accepted 0x10 = 16.
fix: Folded into the AUD-03 shared contract: declared min/max enforced on every entry path, the complete-integer grammar applied, the seven unbounded modules bounded at 12 with measured justification, and a run() gate that programmatic callers cannot bypass.
verified: 11 bound-escape probes all rejected with the correct field key; accepted boundaries (hamilton nV=7 exhaustive negative at 5,873 frames, warshall nV=12, recfactorial n=12 and n=0) still work.

title: medianOfThree comparisons were invisible unless they swapped
found: Raised by a parallel review stream and confirmed against the displayed source.
detail: The q3 trace emitted a frame only when a gt() test caused a swap, so a learner stepping through never saw a comparison evaluate false - on sorted input 7 of 9 tests were invisible. The displayed source shows three unconditional `if (gt(...)) swap(...)` statements, so trace and source disagreed, and the timeline under-reported comparisons (11/14/18 frames against 18/19/24 source comparisons).
fix: Every one of the three tests now emits a frame showing its boolean outcome, with a separate frame when it swaps.
verified: q3 now shows 9/9/12 medianOfThree test frames of which 7/5/6 evaluate false. Oracles 2920/2920 unaffected; default frames 1912 -> 1924, explained.

title: A blank scalar field was silently reinterpreted as zero
found: Same field sweep.
detail: Empty and whitespace-only values reached Number(""), which is 0, so a blank target silently became a search for 0 and a blank recfactorial n silently became the base case. The commission explicitly forbids reinterpreting empty text as zero unless the field defines that convention.
fix: parseIntScalar rejects blank with "A blank field is not treated as 0." Blank LIST fields still mean the empty list, which is a documented and useful boundary case - an empty array is sorted.
verified: Blank scalars rejected with a field key; blank and singleton list inputs still produce valid traces.

title: Hexadecimal and exponent literals were accepted as integers
found: Same field sweep.
detail: Number() accepts "0x10" as 16 and "1e3" as 1000, so both passed Number.isInteger and entered algorithms as silent surprises - and bypassed declared maxima.
fix: One complete-integer token grammar, identical to the grammar parseInts already enforced for lists, so a scalar and a list field accept exactly the same tokens.
verified: Rejected across every affected module; "+23" and "-3" still accepted.

title: The generated topic index had no generator and went stale
found: While changing block titles for CUR-MOD-02.
detail: assets/topics.js is generated data whose producer lived in a private assurance package, so any change to a module's blocks left the search keywords and counts stale. After the content work, coursemap's line count was 93 against an actual 181, four graph modules' counts were stale, and the audited inventory check reports a mismatch against topic.l.
fix: tools/sync_topic_index.cjs regenerates the fields whose derivation is exactly known (k, b, l), verified to reproduce the audited baseline 68/68 for b and l and 67/68 for k. Only coursemap's curated KEYWORDS are preserved; its derived counts are not, which is what had gone stale. The editorial fields n, g, p and s are not regenerated because s comes from an undocumented heuristic and inventing a replacement would change search behaviour without evidence.
verified: A no-op on the pristine baseline and on the successor before the title changes; afterwards it corrected 8 fields. It is a gate in the release pipeline.

title: Displayed C diverged from compiled C, and the audited parity script cannot detect it
found: Flagged by a parallel stream and then measured with the audited comparison script.
detail: The eleven Graph ADTs exist twice: as compilable .c files and as template-literal constants the browser displays. On the baseline they were token-identical 11/11 (never byte-identical, because each copy carries a different leading comment). After the .c files were corrected, the token match fell to 0/11 - the learner would have been shown code that was not the code being compiled and sanitizer-tested, failing AUD-14 acceptance. Separately, reproduce/curriculum/compare_displayed_c.cjs CANNOT judge a successor at all: it loads the displayed side from a frozen source_block_inventory.json captured at the audited commit, so it reports 0/11 regardless of whether the tree is consistent.
fix: tools/sync_displayed_c.cjs regenerates each displayed body from its mapped .c file while keeping that copy's own provenance header, with correct template-literal escaping for the backslashes inside C string literals. tests/displayed_c_parity.test.cjs reads BOTH sides live and is the successor gate; the audited script is preserved unchanged.
verified: The sync tool is a verified no-op on the pristine baseline, which proves the header/body split and escaping reproduce the original exactly. Parity restored to 11/11; the new gate scores 16/16 on the successor and 15/16 on the baseline, failing only the assert check, so it discriminates.

title: All eleven C files failed the project's own strict flags under -DNDEBUG
found: Independently verifying a characterisation claim.
detail: All 11 compile cleanly with the documented strict flags, but ALL 11 FAIL the same command with -DNDEBUG added: "validVertex defined but not used". That is not a warning quirk - it proves every vertex check lived inside assert(), so the entire release configuration had NO input validation.
fix: Public preconditions were moved out of assert() into unconditional checks using each file's existing fprintf(stderr)/exit convention. assert() now appears in zero of the 11 files, so -DNDEBUG removes nothing.
verified: 11/11 compile with ZERO diagnostics both with and without -DNDEBUG (baseline: 0/11 with -DNDEBUG). The audited harness still passes 11/11 strict compiles and 11/11 sanitizer runs at 18,436 operations and 4,046,863 checks - identical to baseline.

title: GraphGetWeight read edges[-1] on a missing edge under NDEBUG
found: Reading the weighted edge-array variants; reproduced under AddressSanitizer.
detail: Both weighted edge arrays did `int i = edgeIndex(g,v,w); assert(i != -1); return g->edges[i].weight;`. With assertions compiled out this is an out-of-bounds read of edges[-1]; ASan reported heap-buffer-overflow, READ of size 8, 8 bytes before a 128-byte region. Neither function validated its vertices at all.
fix: An unconditional missing-edge check that fails loudly, plus the vertex validation both functions lacked.
verified: Unreachable in both builds; covered by the driver suite's fatal-absent-weight stage, required to exit 1 in both configurations.

title: The NO_EDGE sentinel could collide with stored data and corrupt nE
found: Reading the weighted matrix variants.
detail: NO_EDGE is -1.0 while the accepted weight domain was constrained only by assert(weight >= 0.0). Under NDEBUG, inserting -1.0 twice gave nE=1 then nE=2 while GraphIsAdjacent stayed 0 - permanent, unrecoverable nE corruption, because GraphRemoveEdge early-returns on an edge it cannot see. The weighted matrices also hid edge-existence AND vertex validation inside one assert(GraphIsAdjacent(...)), so under NDEBUG an absent edge silently returned -1.0 as a weight.
fix: Weight-domain validation made unconditional and written so it rejects negatives and NaN; existence and vertex checks separated and made unconditional. NO_EDGE is now storage-only and never returned as a weight.
verified: Driver suite fatal-negative-weight and fatal-absent-weight stages exit 1 in both builds; sanitizer and LeakSanitizer runs clean.

title: GraphShow output format differs across variants sharing one declaration
disposition: confirmed; documented as a legitimate difference, not changed
found: Comparing printf counts across the eleven files (7, 5, 3, 3, 1, ...).
detail: The shared declaration fixes the signature, not the format, and the bodies genuinely differ by representation (adjacency rows versus edge tuples). No authoritative source defines one format.
fix: DOCUMENTED per variant in the C library matrix with an explicit warning never to diff one variant's output against another's. Deliberately NOT unified: the commission says characterise first and do not standardise for uniformity without confirming the intended teaching contract.
verified: n/a - a recorded contract difference.

title: The bridge build was not relocatable
found: The deliberate AUD-12 negative test, run in a relocated copy.
detail: bridges_c/build.sh hard-coded ../../baseline_pristine/memorise_graph_c, so 14 target runs failed with missing-path errors whenever the assurance package was extracted anywhere else - exactly what a handoff does. The commission requires relocatable paths and identified external dependencies.
fix: The pinned ADT copy is now an explicitly optional external dependency, overridable with DSA_PINNED_ADT. When absent, the pinned half of the matrix is recorded as SKIPPED - never counted as a pass - and the build does not fail, because the product half is the gate that matters.
verified: In place: full matrix, exit 0. Relocated with no pinned copy: product matrix runs, pinned half explicitly skipped with instructions, exit 0.

title: Fourteen coverage capabilities have no working destination
found: Splitting the 93 coverage rows into 181 per-capability records and executing each destination.
detail: Four are MISSING: radix key padding (the module refuses mixed-width keys), hash-table resizing (the displayed source is literally printf("warning: resize not implemented!")), union-find (closed separately as CUR-MOD-05) and sorting motivation. Ten are PARTIAL, including periodic rebalancing (one frame of prose against global rebalancing's 15-frame trace), backshift deletion, clustering, AVL search with no standalone destination, and spanning-forest structure asserted in one closing sentence with no edges marked.
fix: All 14 now have a working destination, built as real lessons rather than closed by weakening any promise. CAP-146 (union-find) was already satisfied and the finding was stale. The other 13 were implemented across three streams: sorting motivation and the Item/key contract as reference sections; radix mixed-width keys, linked-list selection and bubble, periodic rebalancing, AVL search, spanning-forest tree edges, hash resize and rehash, backshift deletion and the clustering report as traces. Delivery mode is recorded honestly per row - a complete reference section stays conceptual-reference rather than being promoted to executable - so the register now reads 124 executable / 46 conceptual-reference / 11 named-only; 181 complete / 0 partial / 0 missing.
verified: Independently re-verified in a real browser by tools/verify_capabilities.cjs, which does not read any report, status field or note wording: for each capability it re-tests the exact condition the original finding recorded and recomputes stated quantities. 14/14 pass, 0 page errors. Measured: radix traces 7 42 318 in 24 frames (recorded as refused); periodic rebalancing 22 frames (recorded as 1); listsorts insertion 26 / selection 54 / bubble 79; components reports V=10, C=4, 6 tree edges and 6 == 10-4; hash numSlots 11 -> 23 with a rehash frame per key; backshift leaves 0 tombstones; the clustering report's longest run of 3 equals 3 recomputed here from the reporting frame's own slot table; 6 of 6 array sorts name Item in their note. tests/coverage_register_parity.test.cjs (1,450 checks, 0 failures) holds the in-app table and the audit register in agreement, and was shown to catch a single reverted letter.

title: Two coverage destinations were mis-linked
found: Verifying every destination rather than trusting the link.
detail: The comparison-macros capability pointed at sortprops, which does not display them - they are block 0 of the six array sorts. "How to design a recursive function" pointed at recfactorial, which has no design-guide block.
fix: Both destinations corrected. These are mis-links, not coverage gaps.
verified: Both now resolve to a destination that actually contains the claimed content.

title: Two supplemental bridges are unreachable or mis-tokenised
found: Bridge matcher review.
detail: The avl-search bridge contains real bool avlSearch(...) C but is unreachable: the matcher keys on displayed block headings and bodies, and no displayed block anywhere contains avlSearch - which also makes it the cheapest way to close the partial AVL-search capability. Separately, the dfs bridge's token list claims dfshaspath and dfsfindpath while its body defines only dfs and dfsRec.
fix: Two halves, handled differently because they are different problems. (a) dfs bridge: dfsHasPath and dfsFindPath are now IMPLEMENTED - a faithful conversion of the PS_DFS_PATH pseudocode using the same predecessor convention as the BFS bridge - in bridges_c/bridges_graph.{c,h}, and the displayed bridge body is synced from that compiled source. The registered claim is honoured rather than deleted. (b) avl-search bridge: left unreachable ON PURPOSE. pairsHtml pairs MANUAL PSEUDOCODE with a C conversion, and the 26T2 manual prints no AVL search in any form, so there is nothing to pair. Flipping the pairing rule to include supplemental C blocks would show the same C in both columns, and relabelling a lecture or supplemental block as manual would fabricate provenance. The capability is instead closed by content: avldel gained an operation field whose search mode traces a supplemental C block that is token-identical to the avl-search bridge body.
verified: test_dfspath compiles clean under -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror and runs under ASan+UBSan+LSan on all three Graph backends: 27,918 / 27,918 / 26,263 checks, 0 failures, every src-dest pair on a bank of generated graphs checked against an independent boolean-relaxation reachability oracle and cross-checked against the dfs() visited array. Mutation controls: removing the predecessor mark segfaults (unbounded recursion); dropping src from the reconstruction produces 3,389 failures. bridges_c/build.sh 13/13 targets PASS across 4 configurations. verify_displayed_bridges.sh reports 0 bridges whose displayed text differs from the compiled text, and the displayed excerpts compile. New gate tests/bridge_c_parity.test.cjs checks the token claim (103 checks, 0 failures) and was shown to catch this exact defect: reverting the dfs body reproduces 2 TOKEN-UNHONOURED failures naming dfshaspath and dfsfindpath.

title: A vertex-target field rejects a stale value when nV is lowered
found: A parallel stream hit it on the new Dijkstra dest field, and it was then traced to pre-existing behaviour.
detail: bfspath and dfspath on the UNMODIFIED baseline already throw when nV is lowered below their dest default, because a vertex target must be a vertex of the graph. The new dijkstra dest field inherits that established convention. The practical effect is that lowering nV requires also lowering dest, with a clear field error in between.
fix: A committed nV edit now clamps any vertex-target field that the new nV has put out of range, to the highest remaining vertex. The fields are DECLARED in modules-registry.js (VERTEX_TARGET_FIELDS) rather than inferred: webcrawl's `max` is a numeric field beside nV that caps visits, not a vertex, and the types are mixed (bfs/dfs/dijkstra declare src and dest as text, bfspath/dfspath as number), so neither a type nor a name rule would be correct. Deliberately narrow: only a committed `change` on nV clamps (clamping on `input` would drive dest to 0 while someone types '12'); only values ABOVE the new maximum move, so a negative stays a reported typo and raising nV never moves a field the student chose; and run() remains the authority for route-supplied and programmatic values. A stale EDGE LIST is deliberately NOT clamped: a vertex target has one correct repair, an edge list has none, and pruning edges would silently delete input the student typed. It is reported precisely instead, against the edges field.
verified: 7 real-browser tests in tests/browser/acceptance.cjs: dest 6 -> 2 when nV drops to 3; src already in range is untouched; the typed edge list is left intact; the now-stale edge list is reported with aria-invalid on the edges field and the message 'edge 1-3 uses a vertex outside 0..2'; with the edges corrected the smaller graph traces normally; raising nV back to 6 leaves dest at 2.

title: Prim and Kruskal differ on disconnected input
disposition: confirmed; documented as a legitimate difference, not changed
found: A stronger MST test than the audited harness provides.
detail: On a 4-vertex graph with two components, Kruskal selects 2 edges (a minimum spanning forest of every component) while Prim selects 1 (a tree of vertex 0's component only). My initial test expected them to agree.
fix: Not changed. Both are correct for their own algorithm - Prim grows from a single source. The difference is documented in the lesson text and the bridge contracts. The commission warns specifically against standardising different valid contracts; my test expectation was corrected instead.
verified: 14 MST assertions, including the distinct disconnected outcomes for each algorithm.

title: The audited A5 singleton-MST check is too weak to protect its own criterion
found: Reading the harness before relying on it.
detail: reproduce_findings asserts only that Kruskal's final note does not START WITH "no mst". That passes for any replacement wording, including one that still fails to produce a spanning tree, and it never checks the vertex count, edge count or total weight the commission requires.
fix: The audited check is preserved unchanged, and a stronger independent suite was added asserting edges == V-1, total weight, and which of the three outcomes was reported, across singleton, single-edge, triangle, disconnected, zero-weight, fractional-weight and negative-weight inputs.
verified: 14 assertions; the weak audited check and the strong successor suite both pass.

title: Three zoom controls failed WCAG 2.5.3 because two layers owned different halves of the label
found: axe-core 4.14.0 sweep of all 8 pages, loaded and after Run (14 audits)
detail: quality-v632.js rewrites the VISIBLE text of the canvas controls to 'Pan locked', 'Zoom 100%' and 'Fit view', while course-enhancements.js and the static markup owned their aria-label ('Unlock visualisation panning', 'Reset visualisation zoom to 100 percent', 'Fit visualisation in the pane'). The accessible name therefore did not contain the text on screen, so a speech-input user reading the button could not activate it. 3 nodes on 7 pages, 21 violation nodes in total.
fix: The accessible name is now derived from the button's own content, which cannot drift from what is on screen, and the state-dependent explanation moved to an sr-only aria-describedby target that course-enhancements.js updates instead of competing for the name.
verified: axe-core: 21 violation nodes -> 0. Behavioural check through the Chromium accessibility tree, now gated in acceptance.cjs: each control's computed accessible name contains its visible text ('Pan locked', 'Zoom 100%', 'Fit view').

title: The zoom readout was an <output>, whose status role is excluded from name-from-content
found: behavioural accessibility-tree probing after the NEW-19 fix (axe reported this page clean)
detail: With the aria-label removed, #zoomReset's accessible name came out as 'Reset zoom' - its title - not 'Zoom 100%'. The readout was <output id="zoomLevel"> inside the button; role=status is excluded from name-from-content, so the button's content contributed nothing and the name fell through to the title. Removing the title left the name EMPTY, which would have been worse. axe-core did not report it: the markup is valid and only the computed name was wrong.
fix: The readout is a plain <span>, so it names the button, and the spoken announcement moved to a separate sr-only <output aria-live="polite" id="zoomAnnounce"> OUTSIDE the control, updated in the same code path that writes the readout, so the live region is kept rather than traded away.
verified: Accessibility-tree name for #zoomReset is now 'Zoom 100%', asserted in acceptance.cjs.

title: The global trace shortcut made the manual-bridge code panes unreachable by keyboard
found: axe-core (scrollable-region-focusable) plus keyboard probing, which found the real cause
detail: The bridge panes hold 470px of C in a 135px column and scroll, but had no tabindex, so axe reported scrollable-region-focusable on the traced graph pages. Adding tabindex was not enough: with focus in a pane, ArrowRight was preventDefault-ed by the document-level trace shortcut and stepped the trace (frameIndex 1 -> 2) while scrollLeft stayed 0, so the off-screen part of the C could not be reached from the keyboard at all. WCAG 2.1.1. The markup is correct, so this half is invisible to a static rule engine.
fix: The panes are focusable regions with accessible names (tabindex=0, role=region, aria-labelledby pointing at their own heading), and the shortcut handler now declines arrow, space, Home and End when focus sits in a focusable container that is scrollable AND currently overflows. The test is deliberately narrow, so a focusable region that fits its content keeps the shortcut.
verified: axe-core: 2 violation nodes -> 0, 14/14 audits clean. Behaviourally gated in acceptance.cjs: body focus steps the trace; pane focus scrolls the pane (scrollLeft 0 -> 40+) and does NOT step; blurring the pane restores stepping.

title: audit_source_mapping.py discovered modules by a bare id pattern and mis-attributed step sites
found: reported by a content stream that hit 49 false positives and worked around it in its own file
detail: The tool found modules with the text pattern id:'<word>' anywhere in a file. Ordinary JavaScript inside a run() body - an object literal such as {id:'NULL'} built while tracing - was read as the start of a new module, and every later .step() site was then attributed to the WRONG module's source blocks. The author worked around it by double-quoting the offending literals, which is the tool bending the content instead of the reverse.
fix: Discovery is anchored to the mod({ call that actually registers a module, and the id must appear in that call's opening window; an id further in is a nested literal, not a registration.
verified: Same result on the real tree (529 step sites, 66 modules, 0 problems). Control: injecting one ordinary {id:'NULL'} into a run() body makes the OLD tool report 11 problems and inflate the site count to 540, while the NEW tool is unaffected (0 problems, 529 sites).

title: Five supplemental bridges are registered but never render, because the manual has no pseudocode for them
found: tools/audit_manual_bridges.cjs, a new real-browser sweep of every module on every page
detail: 11 manual pairs render across the app and 9 bridges match. avl-search, components, undirected-cycle, hamiltonian-path and hamiltonian-circuit never match, because pairsHtml pairs only MANUAL PSEUDOCODE blocks and the 26T2 manual contains no pseudocode for those routines - the corresponding lessons are lecture-sourced. Exactly one manual pseudocode block exists in the whole app (BFS).
fix: Not changed, and deliberately so. Relabelling lecture or supplemental blocks as manual would fabricate provenance, and widening the pairing rule would make the panel's own statement ('the pseudocode is in the 26T2 manual, this C conversion is not') false. Where the C is worth showing, the honest route is the lesson itself, which is what avldel now does for avlSearch. The audit tool reports the unmatched set every run so the situation stays visible rather than silent.
verified: audit_manual_bridges.cjs: 11 pairs rendered, 9 bridges matched, 0 problems, 0 page errors; no rendered pair shows a conversion missing the routine its pseudocode names.

title: Every page hard-codes the original publication origin in four absolute URLs
found: building the deployable site folder
detail: Each of the 8 pages carries rel=canonical, og:url, og:image and twitter:image pointing at https://asgardianhunter2301.github.io/dsa_guide - 32 absolute URLs in total. The app itself is fully relative and runs correctly from any path, but on a new host a stale rel=canonical tells search engines the real copy is elsewhere, and the social preview points at a file on the old domain.
fix: tools/build_site.cjs takes --base-url=<origin> and rewrites all 32. Without it the existing values are LEFT ALONE and reported on every build, because rewriting them to a guessed origin would be worse than leaving a value the publisher can see and decide about. Choosing the published origin is the owner's decision, so no default was invented.
verified: Default build reports 32 URLs still naming the original origin. A build with --base-url=https://example.org/comp2521/ rewrites 32 and yields rel=canonical href="https://example.org/comp2521/index.html".
disposition: confirmed; tooling supplied, origin choice reserved for the owner

title: Three of seven convention cards described recalled course conventions rather than the code the tracer runs
found: writing the theory register, then independent verification against the executing source by the main session and, separately, by the area author
detail:
The conventions table in assets/corpus-theory.js was first written from conventions recorded in earlier study material rather than from this tracer. THREE of the seven were wrong about what the app executes, and a fourth described a case the app cannot produce.

(a) chainOrder claimed chains are kept in ASCENDING key order. They are not. `doInsert` in modules-hashing.js has exactly three branches - create at NULL, update on an equal key, otherwise recurse into `list->next` - with NO ordering comparison, so a new key is appended at the TAIL and a chain sits in ARRIVAL order. Inserting 23, 12, 1 leaves the chain [12, 1]; ascending order would have left [1, 12]. The supplemental resize is a second, opposite behaviour: it relinks with `curr->next = newSlots[j]; newSlots[j] = curr;`, which is head insertion, so a rehash REVERSES a chain.

(b) heapIndexing claimed the heap ADT is 1-based with heap sort as the only 0-based exception. Two bases coexist and the exception is a PAIR: the priority-queue ADT is 1-based (`2 * i` children, root `items[1]`, index 0 unused) while BOTH heapify and heap sort are 0-based (`2 * i + 1` children, `(i - 1) / 2` parent, every frame declaring `base: 0`).

(c) dfsStack claimed neighbours are pushed in DECREASING order so the smallest pops first. The tracer pushes in ASCENDING vertex order - `for (w = 0; w < nV; w++) ... S.push(w)` - so the HIGHEST-numbered unvisited neighbour pops first, the opposite of the recursive version. On the star `0-1, 0-2, 0-3, 0-4` the trace pushes 1, 2, 3, 4 and pops 4, 3, 2, 1. The card's three other claims - mark on pop, skip an already-visited pop, a vertex on the stack more than once - all held exactly.

(d) warshallDiagonal said the diagonal is true for a vertex on a cycle OR carrying a self-loop. The self-loop half cannot occur: parseGraph rejects `0-0` with "self loop 0-0 is not supported by this course graph model", so the card described a case no reader can reproduce.

This is the failure the commission targets - teaching one thing while executing another - introduced by the very table meant to prevent it. Three independent area authors each caught the card covering their own area, which is why the discipline of writing against the running code rather than from memory is what found all four.
fix: All four cards rewritten to state what the code does, verified line by line rather than recalled. chainOrder states tail append, arrival order and the resize reversal; heapIndexing states that two bases coexist, that the base must be read off the module rather than assumed, and gives both sets of formulas; dfsStack states ascending push with the highest neighbour popping first and names the contrast with recursive DFS; warshallDiagonal drops the unreachable self-loop case and gives a reproducible example instead. The topic entries were written against the code and already said the right thing, so correcting the cards removed contradictions the `hash` and `dfsiter` panels were showing between their own prose and their convention card.
verified: Verified from both directions for each. Source: `doInsert`'s three branches contain no key comparison; the rehash loop head-inserts; modules-heaps-tries.js uses `2 * i` while corpus-hashing-heaps.js uses `2 * i + 1` and `(i - 1) / 2`; the DFS push loop runs `w` upward. Running tracer: inserting 23, 12, 1 gives chain [12, 1]; heapify and heapsort frames declare `base: 0` with index 2 taking left child 5, while pq puts the root at `items[1]`; the star graph pushes 1,2,3,4 and pops 4,3,2,1; `0-0` is rejected; and Warshall on `0>1, 1>2, 2>3, 2>0` returns a diagonal of true, true, true, false, matching the replacement card exactly. The `hash` and `dfsiter` panels now show no contradiction, with no page errors. tests/theory_register.test.cjs passes 2,544 of 2,544 checks at 68 of 68 coverage.

title: The tracer’s chain order may differ from what the course teaches, which only the owner can settle
found: following NEW-25
detail: Earlier study material prepared for this course recorded ASCENDING-ORDER CHAINS as the course convention for separate chaining. This tracer appends at the tail, giving arrival order (NEW-25). Both cannot describe the same course. Which one is right is not checkable here: the 21 declared original course documents are absent from this repository, so nothing in the tree can confirm what the course actually teaches.
fix: Not changed, deliberately. Altering `doInsert` to sort chains would change executed behaviour on the owner's say-so alone, and rewriting the convention card to claim ascending order would restore exactly the defect NEW-25 removed. The card states what the tracer executes and names the alternative ('chains kept sorted by key') as something seen elsewhere, so a reader comparing against their own material sees the difference rather than being told the tracer is authoritative.
verified: The tracer's behaviour is established beyond doubt (see NEW-25). What the course teaches is not established and is recorded as unresolved rather than assumed.
disposition: confirmed; OPEN - owner decision required (what the course teaches cannot be verified here)

title: The sorting-work register taught a false cause for selection sort being unstable
found: writing the theory register for the sorting area; the claim was then checked against the running tracer
detail: assets/course-enhancements.js stated, for selection sort on repeated keys: "The strict lt test simply keeps the earlier of two equal keys as the running minimum, which is why selection sort is unstable." The first half is true and the conclusion does not follow from it — it is backwards. Keeping the EARLIER of two equal keys as the running minimum is the stability-PRESERVING choice; if the comparison were the cause, a non-strict test would be the fix, and it is not. The instability comes from the long-range swap: `swap(items, i, min)` carries `items[i]` across the whole unsorted region, past any equal key lying between `i` and `min`. A student who learned the stated reason would look for the defect in the wrong statement.
